source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    For Linux:
   - Run GpuTest of Furmark stress test for 4 hours.
For Windows:
   - Run Burnin test of 2D graphic and 3D graphic for 4 hours.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. The on-board VGA should still be detected after stress.
2. System should be OK and no error message after stress.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "glxinfo -B 2>&1 | head -40; echo ---; glxgears -info 2>&1 & sleep 10; kill %1 2>/dev/null 2>&1"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL glxinfo + a short glxgears run so the user confirms VGA/GPU renders under stress without error; a long visual stress needs a person to watch for artifacts.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: display tests need a physical monitor head + a person to observe rendering; agent runs the read-only/headless probe for mode/status evidence only.

original_test_intent: Run the specified four-hour graphics workload on the applicable Linux GpuTest/FurMark or Windows BurnIn 2D/3D path, then verify the onboard VGA remains detected and the system has no unexpected error messages.
original_method: Use the owner-approved build and parameters of the named OS-specific graphics stress tool for 240 minutes, capture complete tool and display/driver/thermal/system events, and perform a post-run onboard-VGA detection and health comparison.
manual_activity: The owner selects the applicable OS/tool build, render parameters, limits and run approval. The source criteria require post-stress detection and error-free health, both of which can be collected automatically; optional visual artifact observation is additional project coverage, not a basis to downgrade capability.
required_inputs: Applicable OS path and exact approved GpuTest/FurMark or BurnIn tool/version/license/provenance
Onboard VGA/ASPEED device, driver, display session/render target and workload parameters
Four-hour approval plus temperature/power, driver error, hang and management stop thresholds
Maintenance window, workload isolation, log storage, KVM/OOB recovery and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Do not install or run an unapproved graphics tool or replace the named four-hour workload with glxgears.
Do not clear logs; capture immutable display/driver/kernel/BMC/SEL baselines and deltas.
Stop on thermal/power threshold, VGA disappearance, driver reset/crash, host hang, render-tool failure or management loss.
Verify the stress process terminates and the console/driver/device recover before service return.
No automatic retry or shortened substitute.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the approved tool, OS/display target, exact four-hour configuration and stop controls.
Run the named workload and collect complete tool, VGA/DRM/driver, thermal/power, kernel and BMC evidence.
Verify post-run onboard-VGA enumeration and system health against the supplied expectations.
Report results/anomalies without issuing the formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Supply/approve the OS/tool/version/parameters, limits and recovery plan.
Optionally add and perform visual artifact monitoring if the project requires coverage beyond the source criteria.
Review the evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not applicable as the test workload: glxinfo plus ten seconds of glxgears is neither four-hour GpuTest/FurMark nor Windows BurnIn and cannot establish the source criteria. Output is also truncated and process control is shell-session fragile.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the original named tool and four-hour duration. Instantiate only the owner-approved package's documented noninteractive or supervised mode and capture full output/status; no generic substitute is proposed.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Linux GpuTest/FurMark, Windows BurnIn 2D/3D, four hours, Attended Time 10 and Machine Time 240 are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Supervise the approved named workload for 240 minutes, timestamp VGA enumeration, render-tool status, driver resets, temperature/power and system events, then repeat the device/driver/connector health inventory after process exit.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The identified onboard VGA/ASPEED device, OS, driver and supported graphics stress package.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record exact stress-tool, driver, OS, BIOS/BMC and device firmware versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project-approved tool documentation and VGA stress plan; no replacement tool/version is asserted.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds deterministic supervision, stop thresholds and pre/post device identity while preserving tool and duration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers the stated detection/error criteria; visual artifact monitoring is an optional additive project requirement, not silently assumed.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: OS/tool build, render parameters, device mapping, limits and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A headless or virtual renderer may bypass the onboard VGA and must not be used unless the approved target mapping proves equivalent coverage.

project_override_considerations: A project may choose Linux or Windows and approve different duration/parameters, but the report claims only that plan and names any omitted OS or reduced 240-minute coverage. Package/parameter approval does not make the core automated workload PARTIAL.
expected_evidence: OS/onboard-VGA/driver/tool identity, approved workload/limits/duration and authorization
Full four-hour stress output/status with timestamps and render-target identity
Pre/during/post VGA/DRM or Windows device/driver detection plus temperature/power telemetry
Kernel/system/BMC/SEL/driver error deltas, process termination and console/management recovery

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Linux and Windows are alternative stated methods with the same four-hour duration and post-stress detection/error criteria. The missing project OS/tool selection is not a contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Tool, OS, render target and thresholds are readiness inputs. The core stress and acceptance data can be automated once supplied.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Reject the ten-second glxgears substitution and its unsupported claim that visual monitoring is required by the source criteria.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain V2's original-tool/duration and safety controls but reclassify PARTIAL to FULLY AUTOMATABLE; keep visual observation only as optional additive coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates automation capability from package/approval readiness and avoids adding an unstated manual criterion.

review_improvement: This review restores the named four-hour workloads and confines acceptance to onboard-VGA detection and system error evidence, while preventing a virtual renderer from silently bypassing the tested VGA path.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike the adjacent resolution and mux cases, this row does not require judging visible artifacts; its criteria are device detection and system errors. Those can be measured programmatically. Therefore manual observation may improve coverage but is not intrinsic, and FULLY AUTOMATABLE is the accurate V3.1 capability.
